questions.question: Which correction fixes: "It work on 80 port, test port 8765"?
options: A. It work on 80 port, test port 8765
B. It working on port 80, test port 8765
C. It works on port 80; test port 8765
D. It works on the 80 port, test the 8765 port
questions.explanation: Third-person singular needs "works"; say "on port 80" (not "on 80 port"). A semicolon separates two related commands.

questions.question: Which best fixes: "are they did not started or crashed?"
options: A. Did they not start, or did they crash?
B. are they did not started or crashed?
C. Are they did not start or crashed?
D. Did they not started or was crashed?
questions.explanation: Use a clean question form: "Did they not start" (base verb after "did") and parallel "did they crash".

questions.question: Which correction fixes: "write a API integration document"?
options: A. writing API integration document
B. write a API integration document
C. write the API integration document an
D. write an API integration document
questions.explanation: Use "an" before a vowel sound; "API" is pronounced /eɪ-piː-aɪ/, so "an API" is correct.

questions.question: Which fixes the spelling in: "How can I deloy qwen-asr on the rockchip board"?
options: A. How can I deployment qwen-asr on the rockchip board
B. How can I deploy Qwen-ASR on the Rockchip board?
C. How can I deloy qwen-asr on the rockchip board
D. How can I deploys qwen-asr on the Rockchip board
questions.explanation: The verb is "deploy" (not "deloy"). Capitalize product names Qwen-ASR and Rockchip; add a question mark.

questions.question: Which fixes: "are there defaut values for new parameters?"
options: A. Is there default value for new parameters?
B. Are there defolt values for new parameters?
C. Are there default values for the new parameters?
D. are there defaut values for new parameters?
questions.explanation: Spell "default" correctly; capitalize the sentence and use "the new parameters" when referring to specific API fields.

questions.question: Which is the most natural way to ask whether a port is reachable on a device?
options: A. Check whether port 8765 is open on the phone.
B. Is the 8765 port opening on the phone?
C. Check if port open 8765 on phone.
D. check if the 8765 port is open on the phone?
questions.explanation: Put the port number after "port" ("port 8765"); use "whether" for yes/no checks and capitalize the sentence.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English: "LLM gateway 监听在哪个端口"
questions.modelAnswer: Which port does the LLM gateway listen on?
questions.explanation: Use "listen on" for a server binding to a port; "LLM gateway" is the subject.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English: "应该是从扩展参数传, 不然, openAI不兼容啊"
questions.modelAnswer: It should be passed via extension parameters; otherwise it won't be OpenAI-compatible.
questions.explanation: "Extension parameters" maps 扩展参数; "OpenAI-compatible" is the standard phrasing for API compatibility.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English: "不管哪种实现, 都要遵循相同的接口设计, 都要提供HTTP接口"
questions.modelAnswer: Regardless of the implementation, both must follow the same interface design and expose HTTP APIs.
questions.explanation: "Regardless of" covers 不管; "expose HTTP APIs" is clearer than literal "provide HTTP interface" in backend docs.

questions.question: Rewrite in clear technical English (from the log): "check if the port is open on the polar-chip board" — specify you mean the llmgate service port after reading the code.
questions.modelAnswer: Check whether the llmgate port is open on the PolarChip board (read the code to confirm the port number).
questions.explanation: Name the service (llmgate), use "whether" for a binary check, and note that the port should be confirmed in code (9091 in today's session).
